title: Create the Illusion of Control
coreMove: Ask calibrated how and what questions that make the other side solve the path forward.
sourcePressure: The source ties this chapter to calibrated questions, collaboration, how questions, defusing conflict, and steering while preserving the other side's agency.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The writer must not turn this into generic open-ended questioning or disguised commands with question marks.

hook: A manager asks a better open-ended question
A coach helps someone find their own answer
Questions are more powerful than statements

exampleSpecs.domain: port crane unloading schedule after a labor shortage
exampleSpecs.audience: a terminal operations lead facing a shipping agent demanding an impossible unload time
exampleSpecs.stakes: reefers may lose power if the schedule is promised without a workable crew plan
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the lead asks how the agent wants to keep refrigerated containers powered if the crane slot stays fixed, making the agent propose a staggered discharge order
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a reefer power cord coiled beside a blinking container stack

exampleSpecs.audience: a charge nurse dealing with a surgeon pressing for a room before sterilization is complete
exampleSpecs.stakes: rushing turnover creates infection risk and staff blame
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the nurse asks what part of the sterile count the surgeon wants documented as skipped, forcing the surgeon to solve for time another way
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a wrapped instrument tray waiting under a blue sterile indicator strip

exampleSpecs.audience: a studio producer trying to keep a publisher from demanding a feature freeze before QA findings are known
exampleSpecs.stakes: the release may ship with a save-corruption bug if the demand is accepted as stated
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the producer asks how the publisher wants to handle refunds if the save bug survives the freeze, shifting the publisher into planning the QA exception
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a bug dashboard filtered to one red save-corruption ticket

exampleSpecs.domain: orchard packing-house contract with a grocery chain
exampleSpecs.audience: a packing-house owner facing a buyer demanding tighter delivery windows
exampleSpecs.stakes: fruit may bruise in staging if the chain refuses flexible dock times
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the owner asks what the buyer would like the packers to do with picked fruit when trucks are held outside the dock window
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a waxed apple tray stamped with a harvest-lot number

exampleSpecs.domain: library digitization rights negotiation with a family archive
exampleSpecs.audience: an archivist trying to move a family trustee from blanket refusal to workable safeguards
exampleSpecs.stakes: fragile letters may stay inaccessible until they physically deteriorate
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the archivist asks what protections would make limited access acceptable, letting the trustee design a redaction and embargo path
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a cotton-gloved hand lifting a brittle letter from an acid-free folder

exampleSpecs.audience: a commissary owner dealing with a truck operator demanding more prep hours
exampleSpecs.stakes: health-code compliance fails if the owner simply says yes to overlapping prep slots
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the owner replaces refusal with 'How would you like us to pass inspection with both trucks using the same wash sink at 6 a.m.?' and the operator suggests a split prep window
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a three-basin wash sink tagged with a health-department sticker

skillTargets: write calibrated how or what questions that preserve agency
distinguish real calibrated questions from disguised commands
analyze how a question transfers problem-solving responsibility
evaluate whether a question defuses conflict or escalates blame

tryThisNowSpec: Take one demand you want to reject and turn it into a how or what question that makes the other person solve the practical consequence of their own request.
sourceAnchorsNote: source contains no named anecdote for this chapter

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: prevents the timestamp+named-protagonist template from dominating the chapter

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm — a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following 'concrete anchor -> abstract rule -> elaboration'
